abstract: Recently, a new model of quantum walk, utilizing recycled coins, was introduced; however little is yet known about its properties. In this paper, we study its behavior on the cycle graph. In particular, we will consider its time averaged distribution and how it is affected by the walk’s “memory parameter” - a real parameter, between zero and eight, which affects the walk’s coin flip operator. Despite an infinite number of different parameters, our analysis provides evidence that only a few produce non-uniform behavior. Our analysis also shows that the initial state, and cycle size modulo four all affect the behavior of this walk. We also prove an interesting relationship between the recycled coin model and a different memory-based quantum walk recently proposed.

specification.problem: Reconstruct the time-averaged position distribution of a discrete-time coined quantum walk on the cycle graph C_N whose coin operator depends on a real 'memory parameter' lambda in [0,8] (the recycled-coin model), and the criterion for deciding whether that distribution is uniform or non-uniform as a function of lambda, the initial state, and N mod 4.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest useful construction: a generic coined quantum walk on the N-cycle with a 2-dimensional coin, a lambda-dependent coin unitary C(lambda) whose explicit form is NOT given by the abstract and is left as an unspecified unitary placeholder, the standard conditional shift, and the time-averaged distribution over T steps compared against the uniform distribution 1/N. Tiny explicit instance (assumed): N = 4 vertices (2 position qubits), 1 coin qubit, T = 8 time steps, initial state |x=0> tensor |c=0>. Out of scope: the exact recycled-coin dynamics (how the coin is 'recycled' rather than reset), the specific functional dependence of the coin on lambda, the classification of which lambda values give non-uniform behavior, the N mod 4 analysis, and the proven relationship to the other memory-based quantum walk.

symbols.meaning: Number of vertices of the cycle graph
Number of position qubits, n = \lceil \log_2 N \rceil
Memory parameter of the recycled-coin walk, controlling the coin flip operator
Coin flip unitary depending on the memory parameter
Conditional shift operator moving the walker along the cycle
Probability of finding the walker at vertex x after t steps
Time-averaged position distribution over the first T steps
Number of time steps included in the time average

equations.label: State space and computational basis
equations.description: Position register encodes the vertex x of the N-cycle as an integer in binary (little-endian, n qubits, values x >= N unused); the coin register is one qubit. Register ordering: position first, coin last.
equations.justification: Standard Hilbert-space structure of a coined discrete-time quantum walk on a degree-2 graph (the cycle).
assumptions: Coin space is 2-dimensional; the recycled-coin model may use a different coin structure not determinable from the abstract.

equations.label: Conditional shift on the cycle
equations.description: Coin value 0 moves the walker one vertex clockwise (+1), coin value 1 moves it counter-clockwise (-1), with modular (periodic) wrap-around on the cycle.
equations.justification: Standard flip-flop-free shift for coined walks on the cycle graph; the modular reduction encodes the cycle topology.
assumptions: Direction convention (c=0 -> +1) is a choice; the paper may use the opposite convention.

equations.label: Parameter-dependent coin and one-step walk operator
equations.latex: U(\lambda) = S\,\big(I_N \otimes C(\lambda)\big),\quad C(\lambda) \in U(2),\ \lambda \in [0,8],\quad |\psi_t\rangle = U(\lambda)^t\,|\psi_0\rangle
equations.description: One step of the walk applies the lambda-dependent coin to the coin register and then the shift; t steps are t repeated applications. The explicit matrix C(lambda) is not given by the abstract and is a placeholder.
equations.abstract_quote: a real parameter, between zero and eight, which affects the walk’s coin flip operator
equations.justification: The abstract states the memory parameter is real in [0,8] and enters through the coin flip operator; the coin-then-shift product structure is the standard form inferred for a coined walk. The recycled-coin mechanism may modify this product structure in ways not inferable here.
assumptions: The walk is time-homogeneous (same U each step).
The recycled-coin dynamics can be written as a single unitary of the form S(I tensor C(lambda)); the actual model may differ.

equations.label: Position distribution at time t
equations.description: Marginal probability of the position register obtained by tracing out (summing over) the coin.
equations.justification: Born rule applied to a computational-basis measurement of the position register.

equations.label: Time-averaged distribution
equations.description: Finite-T time average (exact arithmetic mean over the first T steps) and its limiting value; the abstract's object of study is the limiting average, which the finite instance only approximates.
equations.abstract_quote: we will consider its time averaged distribution
equations.justification: Standard definition of the time-averaged (Cesàro) distribution of a quantum walk, which is what 'time averaged distribution' conventionally denotes.
assumptions: The paper uses the standard Cesàro mean; the averaging window convention (0..T-1 vs 1..T) is a choice.

equations.label: Uniformity criterion
equations.description: Non-uniform behavior means the limiting time average deviates from 1/N on some vertex; Delta_T is a finite-T total-variation-style diagnostic (approximation to the limiting statement).
equations.abstract_quote: only a few produce non-uniform behavior
equations.justification: The abstract contrasts uniform and non-uniform time-averaged behavior; comparison against the uniform distribution 1/N on N vertices is the natural formalization.
assumptions: The deviation diagnostic Delta_T is a proposed measure, not one stated in the abstract.

registers.name: position
registers.role: Encodes the vertex x of the cycle as an unsigned integer (little-endian); shift acts as modular +/-1 adder

registers.name: coin
registers.role: Direction of travel; acted on by C(lambda) and controls the shift

specification.initial_state: |\psi_0\rangle = |x=0\rangle \otimes |c=0\rangle (assumed localized instance; the abstract states the initial state matters but does not specify which initial states are studied)

steps.description: Prepare the position register in |0> and the coin register in |0> (assumed initial state).
For each time t in {0,...,T-1}: apply U(lambda) = S(I tensor C(lambda)) t times to the initial state, using the chosen placeholder coin C(lambda) and the modular shift.
Measure the position register in the computational basis to estimate P_t(x) for each t.
Average the estimated P_t(x) over t = 0..T-1 to obtain the finite-T time-averaged distribution and compare with 1/N.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of the n position qubits after t steps (coin register discarded), repeated over shots for each t in 0..T-1 to estimate P_t(x).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate P_t(x) from shot frequencies for each t, form the arithmetic mean over t (eq_5), compute Delta_T (eq_6), and repeat for a grid of lambda values in [0,8], several initial states, and cycle sizes N with different residues mod 4 to probe the dependence described in the abstract.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the tiny instance N = 4, T = 8, initial state |0>|0> is a reconstruction choice.

The recycled-coin walk is modeled as a standard coined walk with a 2-dimensional coin and a time-homogeneous step operator; the true recycled-coin mechanism may require a different coin space or coupling and cannot be recovered from the abstract.
C(lambda) is treated as an unspecified 2x2 unitary placeholder; no explicit lambda-dependence is invented.
Position encoding is unsigned little-endian binary with modular wrap-around; the direction convention c=0 -> +1 is a choice.
missing_information: Explicit form of the coin flip operator C(lambda) and how the real parameter lambda in [0,8] enters it.
Precise definition of the 'recycled coin' dynamics (how the coin is reused/recycled rather than reset, and the dimension of the coin space).
Which specific lambda values yield non-uniform time-averaged behavior and the corresponding analytical or numerical evidence.
The initial states considered and the exact dependence of the results on cycle size N modulo 4.
The statement and proof of the relationship between the recycled-coin model and the other memory-based quantum walk.
